reasoning: Set A is closer to the ground truth and better built. It plans all three stages as the user described them: a circular tank where fish survive as long as possible with limited vision, REINFORCE then PPO, and a single learning predator. It gets the self-play concept right with an opponent pool, saved generations, a cross-play table and ratings, and its RL details are careful (truncation kept separate from termination for bootstrapping, the library PPO's defaults matched). Its roadmap has one milestone per stage with correct Depends cells. M1 is a full Snake vertical slice: training, evaluation, the reference, ablations and replay. Its dependency graph is clean. Its main weaknesses are leftover migration text ('adopted before M1 is built', CORE-06's 'after the core's interface revision', 'TC-01–TC-49 don't change', Replan notes), a brief that says 'Not doing: Designing future environments now' while the spec designs all three, and some packets that leave out types the task needs. Set B departs from the ground truth. Its tank is a square, fish respawn and score 'hits per fish' (lower is better) instead of survival time, predator-prey has 2 predators, and it drops the opponent pool, so the self-play concept is never taught. Its M1 ships a DQN spine with 'no replay buffer or target net'. Replay, the reference check and 'snake beats baselines' are pushed into a carved-off M2 ('See, check and explain'), which is the kind of leftover milestone the rubric penalizes. Spines also write other owners' modules (train_loop builds runlog.RunWriter; the DQN spine builds methods.factory), and the PL-03 wiring task runs on a fake until the system task swaps it out. B's contract and replay design are solid, but it scores lower on content and layout.

Careful RL design: tabular then DQN then CNN ladder, ablations, REINFORCE vs PPO, truncation vs termination handled correctly, settings mapped to the reference library
One milestone per stage with correct dependencies; M1 is a complete Snake slice including replay and the library comparison
